summary: A Readymag poster-scroll for Nouvelle Noire's Pivot Grotesk: giant black type and Lottie pictograms (globe, spiral, sunburst, striped sphere) on pale grey, with every line labelled by its point size in tiny red, then a black 'journey around the core' chapter of archival sources (Muybridge, Haeckel, Diderot) that ends in construction diagrams of the two principles, radial lines and the logarithmic spiral. Specimen sections (text waterfall with a Day/Night switch, categorised glyph grid with Unicode and feature tags) lead to pill-shaped BUY / TRY / SPECIMEN PDF buttons.

instances.look: 'Pivot' in Black filling the full width on pale grey, with three big black pictograms below (a globe with meridians, a spiral, a striped half-lit sphere) and a tiny red '119 pt' label in the left margin
instances.ux: No scroll cue; the fixed red link row (Pivot Grotesk, Buy Fonts, Trial Fonts, Specimen PDF, Nouvelle Noire) sits across the top
instances.learn: Pair the wordmark with a small set of pictograms that encode the concept (rotation, spirals, orbit): the theme is legible before any copy

instances.variantDefinition: The same running text set at a descending series of labelled sizes, from a display headline down to caption size, often in several weights side by side, to show how the family reads at every size; sometimes with a light/dark switch
instances.look: Sticky red pill switch 'Day | Night' over 'Ballet of Day and Night.' in huge Bold, then the same lyrical text about the Earth's rotation at 48, 24, 18, 12, 10, 8 and 6 pt, first as one wide paragraph, then two, three and four columns in different weights, each size marked in red in the margin; it ends with 'Any flat earthers here?'

instances.learn: Step the text size down while multiplying columns and weights: one screen proves headline, body and footnote, and a Day/Night switch tests both polarities

instances.look: Opened by a giant 'G' beside a striped sphere and 'ABC abc&' at 420 pt, then 'Character Set' with a red note and a sticky pill switch 'Standard Character Set | 🌐 | Basic Character Set'; below, the whole set in small black glyphs over red Unicode codes, grouped under red headings (Uppercase, Uppercase Greek, Lowercase, Ligatures, Figures, Fractions, Punctuation, Symbols, Arrows, Superiors, Marks, Case Sensitive Forms, Stylistic Sets)
instances.ux: The two pills swap the grid between the standard and basic character sets; figure and stylistic-set rows carry their feature tag (onum, tnum, zero, sups, case, ss01–ss04) instead of a code
instances.learn: Label each cell with its Unicode, or with the OpenType tag for alternates: the grid documents the features as well as the coverage
